page: Microsoft Azure M12ds_v3 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the MDSMediumMemoryv3 family, managed by Microsoft Hyper-V. The server provision provides 12 dedicated vCPUs based on the x86_64 Intel processor architecture. With 240.0 GB of system RAM, it delivers an expansive memory-to-vCPU allocation of 20.0 GB per core, targeting scenarios where working data sets must reside in fast volatile memory.

For local disk requirements, the instance includes 429 GB of local SSD temporary storage and is capable of attaching Premium Storage. It contains no onboard GPUs and offers no complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The configuration relies on dedicated CPU resources to ensure steady execution without compute contention from neighboring tenant workloads.

Cost efficiency is centered on high memory density rather than raw compute parallelism or hardware acceleration. Deploying 240 GB of RAM against 12 vCPUs offers a balanced tradeoff for memory-bound applications that do not require massive compute threads, avoiding expenditure on surplus CPU cores to achieve large memory limits. Workloads suited for this virtual machine include large in-memory caching layers, medium-scale relational databases, enterprise transactional systems, and ETL pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure M12ds_v3 is a memory-optimized virtual machine from the MDSMediumMemoryv3 family designed for data-intensive enterprise tasks. Powered by an x86_64 Intel processor with 12 dedicated vCPUs, it is characterized by an extensive memory provision of 240.0 GB of RAM, equating to 20.0 GB per vCPU. Storage architecture features 429 GB of local SSD capacity alongside support for Azure Premium Storage. The instance does not include graphics accelerators or complimentary public IPv4 addresses. By concentrating a large memory pool into a moderate vCPU count, the M12ds_v3 provides an efficient profile for memory-constrained workloads without demanding superfluous compute cores. It is designed specifically for running enterprise in-memory caches, relational database management systems, transactional platforms, and memory-heavy analytics pipelines requiring steady, dedicated CPU performance.
